sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Multi-Channel Omni-Helpdesk and Conversational Bot Cloud

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic heritage), unitary national legal system with no sub-state tax variation
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital, signed 17 July 1994, as supplemented by the OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) ratified by Luxembourg
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) investment promotion and protection agreements applicable to Luxembourg, including the BLEU-China BIT framework
EU Internal Market Treaties and the EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 December 2020, pending ratification)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML Law); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 26 October 2020 and the Law of 25 November 2020; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies; CSSF Circulars 18/698 and 20/744 regarding AML/CFT professional obligations; Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 on cash controls.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted legitimate-interest access for AML obliged entities, journalists and NGOs; no fully public UBO register)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: SCSp Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société / Statuts de la Société en Commandite Spéciale)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All founding partners, acting collectively; notarial deed required only where real property is contributed to the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No mandatory notarization for standard contribution of cash or securities; if executed outside Luxembourg, apostille under the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing or Equivalent Registry Extract of each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry or competent commercial registrar of the corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a party to the Hague Convention; otherwise consular legalization through the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate having jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Luxembourg general partner or local incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly authorised director or managing partner of each corporate partner, or each individual partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization depending on the country of execution; if the POA is not in French, German or Luxembourgish, a sworn translation is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of Identity and Residential Address for all Ultimate Beneficial Owners (passport / national ID and recent utility or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or national ID issuing authority and utility provider or credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copies by a Luxembourg notary, registered auditor, bank, or licensed fiduciary; apostille/consular legalization may be demanded by the notary or fiduciary where the UBO resides in a non-EU jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to acceptance, every UBO, partner, director and authorized signatory must be screened against at least the following: United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List, European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, Luxembourg asset freezing list, OFAC SDN list, FATF public statements and internal adverse media/PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where any UBO is a Politically Exposed Person under Article 4(1)(10) of the Luxembourg AML Law. Re-screening of all UBOs must be performed every 90 days and on any material event (ownership change, new partner or adverse media hit).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the Guichet Unique, https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SCSp name must be written in Latin script (A-Z, no Cyrillic, Arabic or ideographic characters are accepted for registration). Non-Latin names must be transliterated and registered in their Latin-alphabet form. The name may be in any language provided it is intelligible and not contrary to Luxembourg public policy or misleading. The statutory suffix 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' must be appended to the name for clarity and legal identification in RCS filings.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg / État / National / Gouvernement (when falsely implying state sponsorship)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed SCSp name is rejected, the applicant may: (1) immediately submit a revised name through the LBR Guichet Unique portal; (2) file a written administrative appeal with the Director of the Luxembourg Business Registers within the time limit stated in the rejection notice, attaching the refusal decision and a new or clarified name; (3) after an adverse administrative decision, bring proceedings before the Luxembourg administrative courts (Tribunal administratif) within the applicable statutory appeal period, represented by a Luxembourg-licensed attorney. A name reservation may be extended for one further 30-day period by written request before the original reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual mailbox or unstaffed PO Box is not permitted as the registered office of an SCSp. The RCS requires a real geographical address in Luxembourg where the registered office is situated and where legal documents may be served. A business centre or licensed fiduciary address may be used where physical reception, mail forwarding and local representation services are provided. For a helpdesk/cloud business with no local employees, a registered-office-only arrangement is legally valid but must be supported by adequate commercial substance where tax treaty benefits, VAT registration or bank account opening are involved.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10%-15% annual likelihood for a low-risk, non-licensed helpdesk SaaS SCSp maintaining a compliant registered office. The inspection risk rises to approximately 30% or more if the SCSp has no local substance, files cross-border service invoices, or the registered address is shared by a large number of inactive entities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance request and availability check with Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory search fee; nominal charge may apply for expedited processing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of the SCSp registration file and entry in the RCS (Trade and Companies Register)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register / LBR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff pursuant to the Grand-Ducal Regulation governing RCS fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the SCSp formation in the RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
UBO declaration filing with the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No separate statutory filing fee; mandatory under the Law of 13 January 2019

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg law firm fee for drafting the SCSp partnership agreement, corporate book and partner consents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark at EUR 250-400 per hour, approximately 6-8 hours for a standard non-regulated SCSp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Optional notarial authentication of the partnership agreement or notarial deed if real estate is contributed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff and disbursements, applicable only where notarization is required or requested by a bank

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization bundle for foreign corporate and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / competent Luxembourg consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedule plus courier costs; Hague Apostille fee approximately EUR 20-40 per certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/UBO screening, PEP and sanctions database verification and due diligence file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed fiduciary or compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-project fixed fee at prevailing Luxembourg market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service for SCSp (annual fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual service contract; market benchmark for a low-risk non-regulated entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax and legal opinion on SCSp pass-through eligibility and DTA/MLI substance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 944-1 to 944-14 (Société en Commandite Spéciale regime introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016, in force 14 August 2016), read with the general partnership provisions (Articles 688 et seq.); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and the Trade Register (RESA) and the Electronic Companies and Associations Gazette, as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial register greffe); official electronic gazette: RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership agreement / instrument of incorporation ('contrat de société') in private writing or notarial deed, with the RCS standard data-capture form, the appointment and acceptance of the responsible person ('personne responsable') and signed powers of attorney; filed electronically via the e-RCS portal as the initial deposit ('1er dépôt').
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SCSp (Article 944-2, Law of 10 August 1915); the partnership agreement freely fixes capital commitments. No mandatory bank escrow or capital blocking attestation is required for incorporation, although cash contributions must be paid on the SCSp's professional bank account to the extent provided in the agreement. The SCSp is not a UCI; CSSF prudential capital rules apply only if an external AIFM is appointed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income taxes. Electronic portals: MyGuichet.lu and the Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu) for entity registration; eTVA portal for VAT return filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through MyGuichet.lu/lbr.lu to obtain the RCSL registration number and the national identification matricule. Step 2 — File the VAT registration application (Formulaire 640) with the AEDT before commencing taxable supplies; the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU followed by 8 digits (e.g., LU12345678). Step 3 — Submit the RCS certificate, partnership agreement identifying the general partner, proof of Luxembourg seat, and anticipated turnover figures; non-resident partners are permitted and no tax representative is required where a Luxembourg-established general partner exists. Step 4 — Where applicable, register separately for the OSS (non-Union scheme) for EU B2C digital services and obtain an ACD income-tax file number (matricule fiscal) for the transparency reporting of partner allocations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; the SCSp is fiscally transparent by default for Luxembourg income tax and net wealth tax purposes — all income, gains, losses, and credits flow through to partners and are taxed at partner level. For VAT purposes, the SCSp is a distinct taxable person (assujetti) insofar as it carries out an economic activity such as helpdesk/SaaS services. No entity-level territorial income taxation applies in the transparent regime; the place of effective management determines only Luxembourg procedural and filing obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections: (i) Article 175bis LIR option — the SCSp may elect, binding for five years, to be taxed as a Luxembourg société de capitaux for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax, subject to the conditions of Article 175bis LIR and ACD guidance; (ii) VAT fiscal unity — election under Article 61 of the Loi TVA to form an assujetti unique with closely related Luxembourg entities; (iii) small-enterprise exemption waiver under Article 57 of the Loi TVA for turnover below EUR 35,000, unavailable for SaaS/helpdesk B2B supplies; (iv) hybrid mismatch documentation and neutralization elections under the ATAD 1/2 implementing law of 21 December 2018. Luxembourg does not operate a 'check-the-box' regime, but partners may file U.S. Form 8832 elections, which interact with Luxembourg tax transparency under reverse-hybrid rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); FX and payment regulation also coordinated with Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and Ministère des Finances
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is within the eurozone, and the euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. No Luxembourg exchange control regime restricts inward or outward capital movements. Profit remittances and distributions by an SCSp to non-resident partners are not subject to withholding tax, provided the partnership is properly registered and the economic substance and beneficial ownership documentation satisfy CSSF/EU anti-money laundering standards. Payment settlement in freely usable foreign currencies is permitted for trade and operating purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender rule or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Luxembourg. Export or service receipts may be retained in any currency in domestic or foreign bank accounts. All cross-border wire transfers require exact purpose codes and comply with EU Regulation 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds and with CSSF anti-money laundering reporting obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with FX and Liquidity Management

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Luxembourg-licensed and EU-passported electronic money institutions and payment institutions, such as licensed EMI subsidiaries of fintech platforms, can support client billings and payment operations for the helpdesk SaaS; however, non-EU offshore EMIs without a Luxembourg/EU passport face rejection under CSSF outsourcing and AML/KYC rules. An SCSp structure requires a dedicated EMI navigation because the partnership is not a classic corporation, and EMI account opening must be reinforced by the partnership agreement, beneficial ownership register, and source-of-funds documentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance of the general partner (or managing shareholder), the ultimate beneficial owners, and the appointed AML compliance contact is generally required during the first account opening at premium and major Luxembourg banks. Remote opening may be available only where the bank applies a full CSSF-compliant digital KYC solution with multilingual video identification, e-signatures, and corroborative documentary checks; but the standard commercial bank practice for an SCSp is one in-person interview or a documentary notarised verification meeting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of the SCSp beneficial ownership chain, especially if the partnership has a discretionary general partner or layered investor structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified partnership agreement, excerpt from the Luxembourg Register of Commercial Companies (RCS), current beneficial ownership declaration submitted under the Luxembourg transparency register law, full identification documents and proof of address for all natural-person ultimate beneficial owners, and a clear multi-level ownership chart to the final natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction routing for initial capital contribution or subscription funds from non-specified wealth sources
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements certified by the bank counsellor, bank statement of the originating account, contract or capital-call notice supporting the transfer, investor identity and passport copies, and an external legal opinion from a Luxembourg law firm attesting to the lawful origin and economic rationale of the funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear operational purpose of the account, artificial mismatch between projected SaaS revenue and treasury movements, or anticipated high-volume Stripe/PayPal settlements without an identified settlement flow
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan for the omni-helpdesk and conversational bot cloud platform, executed SaaS agreements or order forms, projected client traffic and revenue volumes, payment processor terms and detailed flow diagrams for inbound settlement from Stripe/PayPal, a share-of-funds explanation for payroll and software infrastructure disbursements, and the SCSp annual financial projections signed by the general partner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed through the SCSp's Luxembourg bank account via SWIFT MT103 from the investing partners. Compliant wire transfer instructions require the use of a correct ECB-style balance-of-payments and money laundering purpose code, e.g. code S.R.06 for capital contribution to investment funds or code S.B.05 for other equity; the bank will require the partnership capital-call memorandum, investor comfort letter, and documented source of funds. Where the investor uses a non-EU bank, the correspondent bank clearance must satisfy EU sanctions screening and SWIFT format enforcement conditions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for the helpdesk SaaS use SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for euro-area vendor settlements, and SWIFT MT103 for cross-border payments to suppliers, software cloud providers, and international labour contractors. For larger procurement milestones, an Irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary LC) may be opened at the Luxembourg bank where the vendor requires payment security, with a compliant presentation package covering invoices, delivery acceptance records, and SaaS service-level achievement milestones.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (outright forwards) for major currency pairs EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, and EUR/JPY
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or illiquid emerging-market currencies where local deliverability is prohibited
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to match long-term subscription revenue in foreign currency with euro-denominated operating cost liabilities
FX swaps for short-term liquidity rebalancing between the operating account and the capital escrow account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS annual data validation declaration (déclaration annuelle / mise à jour des inscriptions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), via the LBR/e-Justice online filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based cycle: confirmation due within one (1) calendar month after the LBR annual validation notice issued on the anniversary of the initial RCS registration; no fixed calendar date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 10,000 under Article 51 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002, prosecuted by the Parquet (Public Prosecutor); recurrent non-compliance exposes the SCSp to court summons, injunctions, and administrative strike-off/radiation proceedings for dormant entities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO annual confirmation and beneficial ownership update (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBOC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RBOC, via the LBR/e-Justice online filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within one (1) month of the transfer or change; annual confirmation is embedded in the RCS annual validation procedure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to three (3) years for deliberate non-disclosure under the Law of 13 January 2019; the LBR blocks the annual validation until UBO data is reconciled; persistent non-filing is reported to the AML supervisory authorities and may support strike-off action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels) – mandatory only if the SCSp loses the small-partnership filing exemption
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Partner approval of annual accounts within six (6) months of the financial year-end and filing within one (1) month of approval; effective filing no later than seven (7) months from the financial year-end (e.g., 31 July following a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 10,000 and court-ordered compliance injunctions; persistent failure triggers Commercial Court strike-off/radiation procedure; audit certification by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé becomes compulsory for entities exceeding large-enterprise thresholds

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit mandatory only when the SCSp qualifies as a 'grande entreprise' by exceeding at least two of three Luxembourg thresholds: balance-sheet total > EUR 20,000,000; net turnover > EUR 40,000,000; average workforce > 250 employees. A non-regulated helpdesk-SaaS SCSp is not statutorily subject to audit; audit is typically imposed by the partnership agreement or investor covenants; regulated financial vehicles (not present here) would require CSSF-mandated audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP per the amended Law of 19 December 2002 and the Luxembourg accounting norms; EU-endorsed IFRS permitted for voluntary consolidated or presentation purposes; the SCSp must maintain separate accounting records reflecting its transparent pass-through status.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must identify all ultimate beneficial owners and lodge a full RBOC declaration at registration. Any transfer of partnership interests, change in control, or change in beneficiary details triggers a mandatory RBOC update within one (1) month. The annual RCS validation serves as the annual UBO confirmation event; after each shareholding transfer, the general partner (gérant commandité) must run a fresh UBO screening and confirm register accuracy before the applicable deadline.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partners and limited partners (registre des associés)
Register of partnership units and transfers (registre des parts)
Minute book of partner and management decisions (registre des procès-verbaux)
Register of managers/gérants and registered office records where maintained

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,500 – 5,500 per year (third-party domiciliation, registered office, and registered agent services for a small non-regulated SCSp)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – 16,000 per engagement if a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises agréé is voluntarily appointed; USD 0 statutory charge where the SCSp remains below mandatory audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp level (fiscally transparent partnership); each partner is taxed on its distributive share. If the SCSp exercises the option for corporate taxation, the aggregate Luxembourg CIT headline rate in Luxembourg City is 24.94% (15% IRC + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP-Box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income, effective rate approx. 5.1%); participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains subject to 10% holding or EUR 1.2m/EUR 6m acquisition cost and 12-month holding period); R&D and investment tax credits up to 13% for qualifying digital and environmental assets; 17-year tax loss carryforward, no carryback.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Modèle 100) - Luxembourg CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax return; filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu / MyTax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 31 May following the calendar fiscal year-end; extendable to 31 December by the ACD upon request; non-calendar year-ends: within 6 months after year-end. Quarterly CIT advance payments fall due on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 11-digit Luxembourg national tax identification number, legal form code, registered office and e-mail of the signing general partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners with a Luxembourg PE enter the PE local registration number and the foreign parent's registered address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting period covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use a 1 January to 31 December calendar year unless the commercial year was changed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach statutory financial statements, partner profit allocation schedule, transfer pricing Local/Master File, and treaty relief requests.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Luxembourg PE's extracted accounts and a schedule of each non-resident partner's distributive share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare taxable net wealth (0.5% rate; EUR 500,000 threshold for transparency); a transparent SCSp attributes net assets to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Corporate partners must aggregate their pro-rata share of SCSp net assets if Luxembourg net wealth tax applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable result of the helpdesk SaaS activity after deductible expenses; for a transparent SCSp this line is informational and profit flows to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Luxembourg-source income attributable to the non-resident partner is entered; avoid double taxation via DTA distributive rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim the 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends/capital gains (subject to statutory shareholding and holding-period conditions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or DTA eligibility; attach Tax Residency Certificate and ownership history.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose royalties, helpdesk service fees and management fees paid to related parties; attach the TP documentation and arm's-length analysis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure charges to non-resident related parties are at arm's length; the ACD may deny deductions if the payee lacks substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a formal notice (mise en demeure), a late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of assessed CIT, default interest at 0.7% per month on arrears, and the ACD's right of arbitrary assessment (taxation d'office). Intentional concealment attracts criminal fines up to 10x the evaded tax and imprisonment of 1 month to 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 540 / 540A (Modèle 540/540A) - Partner-level Luxembourg personal income tax return; filed via MyGuichet.lu / MyTax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May following the tax year for resident individuals; extension to 31 December for taxpayers with commercial or partnership income when filed electronically; non-residents generally file Form 540A or a specific non-resident return with the same 31 May deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sur name, first name, address, date of birth and Luxembourg personal tax identification number (may be same as matricule).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners enter country of residence, foreign TIN and, where applicable, the name of the appointed Luxembourg tax representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Distributive share of the SCSp's net income derived from the multi-channel helpdesk and conversational bot cloud business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Luxembourg-source share only; apply DTA rules to determine whether the income is attributable to a Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim a deduction or tax credit for foreign taxes imposed on the same SCSp income to avoid economic double taxation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Residents of treaty states claim relief under DTA articles for income and capital; attach computation schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 243 - Capital gains on partnership interest
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gains or losses on disposal of SCSp interests or on liquidation of the partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Check whether the applicable DTA assigns taxing rights to the partner's residence state; Luxembourg may retain rights over Luxembourg immovable property.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare any Luxembourg withholding tax suffered on prior distributions and claim a refund under Form 721.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a Tax Residency Certificate for the relevant year and proof of beneficial ownership.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% surcharge on assessment, 0.7% monthly interest, arbitrary assessment; repeated non-filing can escalate to criminal tax fraud charges. Non-residents face direct assessment on the Luxembourg tax representative if the return is not filed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 721 (Modèle 721) - Application for refund or relief from Luxembourg withholding tax under a Double Tax Agreement; filed with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 5 years from the end of the calendar year in which the withholding tax was levied or the income became taxable; no refund is granted after the statute of limitations expires.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address, tax identification number and date of incorporation of the partner seeking the refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide an original or certified copy of the Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty state for the relevant income year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Type of income (dividends, interest, royalties) and gross amount, with the amount of Luxembourg tax withheld by the paying agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the dividend voucher, interest statement or royalty contract and proof of the actual Luxembourg withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cite the relevant LU treaty article (dividends, interest, royalties), the reduced rate applied or exemption claimed, and the legal basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Certify beneficial ownership; for dividends, evidence of the minimum holding percentage (e.g., 10%) and 12-month holding period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose the direct and indirect chain of ownership from the SCSp to the ultimate beneficial owner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the SCSp partnership agreement and share register to enable the ACD's anti-abuse review.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete claims are time-barred and rejected; no interest is paid on refunds; false declarations expose the applicant to fraud penalties, including fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax for corporate distributions. Distributions by a fiscally transparent SCSp are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at the partnership level; the 15% rate applies only where the SCSp has opted into corporate taxation or where a Luxembourg corporate partner redistributes dividends. EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive: 0%; LU treaty rates: generally 0%-5%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from a DTA, the beneficial owner must (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its state of residence, (ii) submit a preliminary exemption request or a refund claim to the ACD using Form 721, (iii) provide evidence of legal and beneficial ownership, and (iv) for dividends, document the qualifying shareholding and holding period. The ACD must approve the reduced rate at source or reimburse the excess withholding within the 5-year statutory limitation period. For transparent SCSp distributions, partners self-report the income in their residence state and no Luxembourg WHT is levied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax. Royalties: 0% statutory withholding tax for payments to most jurisdictions; a 20% withholding tax applies to royalties and similar IP-related fees paid to non-cooperative or harmful tax jurisdictions (effective 1 January 2021). Under Luxembourg DTAs, interest rates range from 0% to 5% and royalty rates range from 0% to 5%, depending on the treaty and the type of IP.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 group consolidated turnover triggers the Master File; Local File is mandatory where cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 100,000 per category (goods, services, financial transactions); Country-by-Country Report applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000. A TP declaration must be attached to the annual tax return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) comparable to UAE, but enforces substance through Article 56bis LIR (arm's length), the judicial GAAR/abuse-of-law doctrine, the Law of 15 March 2020 and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 17 March 2020 on shell entities, DAC6 reporting, ATAD and MLI provisions. The SCSp must maintain real economic substance (local office, qualified helpdesk staff, board management in Luxembourg, commercial activities, and local decision-making); otherwise the ACD may recharacterise profits, deny treaty benefits, impose fines up to EUR 250,000 and apply shell-entity notification obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and tax fraud (fraude fiscale)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of helpdesk SaaS revenue, omission of partner distributions, false accounting entries or artificial profit shifting to zero-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under Luxembourg tax and criminal law: imprisonment of 1 month to 5 years, fines up to 10x the evaded tax (statutory maximum EUR 1,000,000), restitution of evaded taxes, plus administrative surcharges of 10%-20% and 0.7% monthly default interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SCSp's general partner (commandité), jointly and severally liable for partnership debts under Art. 155-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915, may be ordered to pay civil restitution; individual managers risk travel bans, professional disqualification and imprisonment where fraud was ordered or tolerated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / absence of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an SCSp as a mailbox entity with no office, employees or genuine IT support activity, solely to channel SaaS royalties or dividends and obtain Luxembourg treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA benefits, reversal of income allocation, application of Luxembourg GAAR, and administrative fines under the 15 March 2020 shell-entity law up to EUR 250,000 for failure to notify or to provide substance information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner can be compelled to discharge the partnership's tax and social debts; directors knowingly designing shell structures face civil liability for the full tax shortfall and criminal prosecution for fraud.
